newsitem.title: USA: Explosives threat in Hollywood is hoax.
newsitem.headline: Explosives threat in Hollywood is hoax.

text.p: Police cordoned off part of Hollywood near the Paramount film studios on Saturday and evacuated thousands of people after a man claimed to have 5,000 pounds (2,275 kg) of explosives in a van parked outside a TV station.
After about 10 hours, police said they had found no explosives in the vehicle and residents were allowed back into their homes.

The man, a 64-year-old businessman from nearby Long Beach who reportedly had a grudge against the Automobile Association of America, surrendered about four hours after parking a white van outside the local KCAL-TV studios.
On Saturay night he was still being interviewed by police, a spokesman said after the all-clear was declared. It was not immediately known if he had been charged.

Even after the man surrendered and reportedly told police it was a hoax, bomb squad officers did not take any chances. They eventually used armoured battering rams to smash open the van's doors and after six more hours established the van contained no explosives.

Hundreds of residents and movie workers at Paramount were told to go to two nearby high schools transformed into evacuation centres by the Red Cross. City buses barricaded roads into the area from Sunset Boulevard in the north to Beverly Boulevard in the south and ramps on and off the Hollywood freeway were blocked off.
